next.host: journal commits made on the branch with qargi release fix VER --record (push goes on under the cut while they stay inside the paths its plan named), or run {verb} with its own plan: shown, and approved anew

cut-fix-outside.rule: A fix recorded on a release branch goes on under the cut's approval only when it stays inside the paths the cut named
cut-fix-outside.why: the cut approved a release, not a change of the code
cut-fix-outside.message: the commits {commits} leave the paths the cut covers

next.lead: run qargi release push VER without the cut's token: its own plan lists every commit and takes the owner's approval
next.host: run qargi release push VER without the cut's token: its own plan lists every commit and takes the owner's approval

release-notes-empty.why: a release with no notes says nothing about what changed
release-notes-empty.message: the unreleased section of the changelog is empty, and no changelog fragment stands in for notes

next.lead: write the notes, pass --allow-empty-notes, or set the answer release.changelog.fragments so that the fragments count as notes
next.host: write the notes, pass --allow-empty-notes, or set the answer release.changelog.fragments so that the fragments count as notes

release-fragments-unfolded.rule: A release branch holds no unfolded changelog fragment when it is pushed or finished
release-fragments-unfolded.why: a fragment left in the directory is a note that never reached the changelog
release-fragments-unfolded.message: {count} changelog fragments are left unfolded, or the released section of the changelog is empty

next.lead: fold them in the fix worktree, commit, then run qargi release fix VER --record
next.host: fold them in the fix worktree, commit, then run qargi release fix VER --record

feature-runs-open.rule: A feature is finished when none of its runs is open
feature-runs-open.why: an open run holds patches that are not taken in
feature-runs-open.message: {count} run(s) of this feature are still open: {runs}

next.lead: take each run in (qargi local verify, then merge it), or close it: qargi local clean RUN once its work is merged (--discard drops it on purpose), qargi local close RUN --applied-by-am when its patches were applied by hand; then run {verb} again
next.host: take each run in (qargi local verify, then merge it), or close it: qargi local clean RUN once its work is merged (--discard drops it on purpose), qargi local close RUN --applied-by-am when its patches were applied by hand; then run {verb} again

methodology-no-flow.rule: A verb of the git-flow shape runs only on a project whose methodology has that flow
methodology-no-flow.why: the feature, release and hotfix verbs, and the others that need develop and master, cut and merge branches a plain methodology does not have, so on such a project they would act on branches that are not there; a methodology whose flow cannot be read is not run as git-flow either, because that would be a guess
methodology-no-flow.message: {verb} is refused: the project follows the {methodology} methodology, which has no feature, release or hotfix flow (its flow is plain, or cannot be read: qargi methodology check)

next.lead: work goes on a branch cut from the project's one long-lived branch: qargi local prepare, run and verify with --base BRANCH, qargi review check, save and apply, qargi local close and clean, and qargi backlog; the feature, release and hotfix verbs belong to a methodology of the git-flow shape
next.host: work goes on a branch cut from the project's one long-lived branch: qargi local prepare, run and verify with --base BRANCH, qargi review check, save and apply, qargi local close and clean, and qargi backlog; the feature, release and hotfix verbs belong to a methodology of the git-flow shape

runtime-unusable.rule: An extra runtime is sealed, local, started by a command, and not the project's own
runtime-unusable.why: qargi local run starts a member of an extra runtime itself, so it must be a definition qargi has reviewed that it can start
runtime-unusable.message: the runtime {name} cannot be enabled as an extra runtime of this project ({why})

next.lead: qargi provider check {name} (a library pack is sealed with qargi provider seal), or choose a runtime that serves the local surface and is started by a command (qargi provider list); the project's own runtime is not an extra one
next.host: qargi provider check {name} (a library pack is sealed with qargi provider seal), or choose a runtime that serves the local surface and is started by a command (qargi provider list); the project's own runtime is not an extra one

runtime-reads-unacknowledged.rule: The owner's approval of a runtime that does not confine reads says so
runtime-reads-unacknowledged.why: a member on such a runtime can read what the account can read, the owner's own sessions among it, and the owner approves that knowingly
runtime-reads-unacknowledged.message: the approval of the runtime {name} does not carry the phrase the plan printed: reads are not confined

next.lead: ask the owner again, showing the plan, and apply with --plan TOKEN (the token is still good) and the owner's own words, which must contain the phrase; do not write the phrase for the owner
next.host: approve again with --plan TOKEN (the token is still good) and words that carry the phrase the plan printed

runtime-barrier-missing.rule: A read-only role needs the barrier of its own runtime; the acceptance of the project's own runtime does not count
runtime-barrier-missing.why: an acceptance was given for one runtime's missing barrier, and another runtime's missing barrier is another risk
runtime-barrier-missing.message: the runtime {name} has no read-only barrier, so a read-only role is refused on it

next.lead: run the read-only role on a runtime that has a barrier (qargi provider show {name} says what its barrier claims), or leave --runtime out
next.host: run the read-only role on a runtime that has a barrier (qargi provider show {name} says what its barrier claims), or leave --runtime out

runtime-not-enabled.rule: A run uses a runtime the project enabled
runtime-not-enabled.why: an extra runtime changes what a member may run on (another barrier, another sign-in), so the owner approves each one for the project, and a request names none that is not approved
runtime-not-enabled.message: the runtime {name} is not enabled for this project, so a request cannot be resolved in it

next.lead: choose the project's own runtime or one it enabled (qargi provider runtimes PROJECT lists them); enabling one is the owner's approval: qargi provider enable PROJECT --runtime {name}
next.host: choose the project's own runtime or one it enabled (qargi provider runtimes PROJECT lists them); enabling one is the owner's approval: qargi provider enable PROJECT --runtime {name}

runtime-profile-model.rule: A profile's model belongs to the runtime the profile is resolved in
runtime-profile-model.why: a model id is the catalog of one runtime; resolved in another it would name a model that runtime does not offer, or run another model than the profile says
runtime-profile-model.message: the profile {profile} names a model that the runtime {name} does not offer

next.lead: give the profile a tier in place of its model (a tier is resolved in the catalog of each runtime), or resolve it in a runtime that offers the model; qargi agent models lists each profile in its runtime
next.host: give the profile a tier in place of its model (a tier is resolved in the catalog of each runtime), or resolve it in a runtime that offers the model; qargi agent models lists each profile in its runtime

runtime-drift.rule: A run starts on the runtime it was prepared for
runtime-drift.why: a run was prepared against one runtime's definition, catalog, barrier and policy, and the owner approved that runtime for the project; started on another, or on the same one changed since, it would run on what nobody looked at
runtime-drift.message: the run was prepared for the runtime {name}, which it can no longer start on ({why})

next.lead: prepare the run again (qargi local prepare, with --runtime {name} if it is still the one to use); not-enabled: the project no longer lists the runtime (qargi provider runtimes PROJECT), not-usable: it is no longer sealed, local or started by a command (qargi provider check {name}), changed: its definition, catalog, profile or policy is not what it was at prepare
next.host: prepare the run again (qargi local prepare, with --runtime {name} if it is still the one to use); not-enabled: the project no longer lists the runtime (qargi provider runtimes PROJECT), not-usable: it is no longer sealed, local or started by a command (qargi provider check {name}), changed: its definition, catalog, profile or policy is not what it was at prepare

runtime-hidden-path.rule: A member sees its clone, contract and OUT
runtime-hidden-path.why: a run whose member would not see what it works with starts and fails in a way that looks like the member's fault: the sandbox of some runtimes hides a place (a /dev of its own hides /dev/shm) that a scratch directory or a run's temporary directory may be in
runtime-hidden-path.message: the member of this run on {name} would not see what it works with: the runtime's sandbox hides the place the run is in

next.lead: prepare the run again with --scratch on another filesystem, for example a directory under your home such as ~/.cache/qargi-runs, or set QARGI_RUN_TMP to a directory on another filesystem
next.host: prepare the run again with --scratch on another filesystem, for example a directory under your home such as ~/.cache/qargi-runs, or set QARGI_RUN_TMP to a directory on another filesystem

ro-write-outside.rule: A read-only run writes only OUT and TMP
ro-write-outside.why: a review that changes the code it reviews is no longer a review
ro-write-outside.message: a read-only run may not write outside OUT and TMP

next.lead: write the report in OUT; to test patches make a copy in TMP and work there
next.host: write the report in OUT; to test patches make a copy in TMP and work there

sites.text: [ro-write-outside] qargi guard: under the read-only class only the report and the manifest in OUT, and the temporary directory (TMP), may be written (PATH is not). A review reads the work and writes its report to OUT.

[ro-write-outside] qargi guard: under the read-only class only OUT and the temporary directory (TMP) are written: nothing in the clone or anywhere else may be changed (WHAT into PATH). A review reads the work and writes its report to OUT.

[ro-write-outside] qargi guard: under the read-only class nothing is written or changed here: no run directory (the place of OUT and of the clone) is found from this directory, so no write can be shown to be the report; run from the clone.

[ro-write-outside] qargi guard: under the read-only class WHAT writes through a directory name that a variable, a substitution or a glob builds (PATH), which the guard cannot read to tell the clone from OUT; write the path out.

ro-second-tree.rule: A read-only run makes no second tree of the clone inside the clone
ro-second-tree.why: a clone or an init made inside the clone, or a worktree added from it, changes the clone a review is held to; the tree is made in TMP
ro-second-tree.message: a read-only run may not make a second tree (clone, init or worktree) inside the clone

next.lead: clone into TMP with git -C TMP clone CLONE x, then work in TMP/x
next.host: clone into TMP with git -C TMP clone CLONE x, then work in TMP/x

sites.text: [ro-second-tree] qargi guard: under the read-only class only OUT and the temporary directory (TMP) are written: nothing in the clone or anywhere else may be changed (git clone|init|worktree into PATH). A review reads the work and writes its report to OUT.

ro-env-restricted.rule: A read-only run does not assign the variables that decide what runs
ro-env-restricted.why: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and the git and loader variables decide which program a command is
ro-env-restricted.message: a read-only run may not assign this variable

next.lead: pass the path as an argument instead of assigning the variable
next.host: pass the path as an argument instead of assigning the variable

sites.text: [ro-env-restricted] qargi guard: under the read-only class NAME may not be assigned (inline, env, export, declare ...): the tools it runs read their programs and options from it, so a read-only member runs with the NAME it was given. A build, vet or test command with the environment it was given is not refused; leave the assignment out.

member-push.why: the lead's branches are the lead's; a member hands patches back

next.lead: return patches in OUT; the lead takes them in
next.host: return patches in OUT; the lead takes them in

sites.text: [member-push] qargi guard: WHAT is not available to an agent. Agents never push; return patches instead.

member-lead-verb.rule: A member does not run the lead's verbs
member-lead-verb.why: the lead's verbs change the project's records, runs and branches
member-lead-verb.message: a member may not run this verb

next.lead: report what you need in your task output; the lead, or the owner for a skill, runs the verb
next.host: report what you need in your task output; the lead, or the owner for a skill, runs the verb

sites.text: [member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi AREA VERB: a verb that a variable or a substitution builds (it could be any of the verbs that change a skill or the marshal) is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi AREA VERB (or qargi import) changes a skill and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi upgrade changes the installed tool and its skills and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi cloud VERB changes which cloud workspace a project uses and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi local run starts the runtime's command for the lead, with the environment it names, and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi AREA[ VERB] is the lead's (it prepares, verifies or removes runs and agents, or dispatches work, with the lead's credentials and its own record) and is not available to an agent; report what you need in your task output. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.
[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: campaign state requires a lead context; only literal campaign check --spec FILE [--json] is available to a member.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: lib/install_record.py of the tool is the install engine install.sh runs: its uninstall and apply remove and relink the skills, agents and files the install records list, and it is the lead's to run; one of the clone you work in stays yours, and a change to the tool's install you report in your task output.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: lib/render.py is the renderer of member definitions and can run the command a definition names; it is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: lib/gated_answers.py stores models.extensions, models.accept_no_barrier and packs.member_skills for the verbs that have a plan token and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.
[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: NAME VERB changes a memory tier and is not available to an agent; propose it in your report.
[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi memory VERB changes a memory tier and is not available to an agent; propose it in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi ref VERB writes the lead's ref journal, which local verify trusts (record --rewrite also moves a branch of the lead's repository), and is the lead's to run; report in your task output a branch you think should be rewritten or noted.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi branch VERB deletes merged branches and the worktrees qargi made (with --remote, branches on origin with the lead's credentials) and is the lead's to run, from a plan and a token; report in your task output which branches are merged.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi changelog VERB rewrites the changelog of a work tree and is the lead's to run; only qargi changelog renumber --check (it writes nothing) is available to an agent; report the duplicate item numbers in your task output.
[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi backlog graph is a read-only query reserved for the lead under the current CLI policy; report graph findings in your task output.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi backlog VERB moves an item out of the backlog file into the dated archive and rewrites the file (from a plan and a token) and is the lead's to run (qargi backlog list only reads and is allowed); report in your task output which backlog items your change finishes, with the evidence.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi upstream status fetches into the lead's repository, which changes the remote-tracking refs that qargi local verify compares and is the lead's to run (qargi upstream review only reads the last fetch and is allowed); report in your task output that the upstream line needs looking at.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi upstream VERB fast-forwards the branch that carries the upstream line (and journals the move), from a plan and a token, and is the lead's to run (qargi upstream review only reads the last fetch and is allowed); report in your task output that the upstream line needs looking at.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project link|unlink changes what the checkout and the runtime's memory directory load (skills, agents, memory) and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project unset removes an answer of the project the lead runs on (the answers qargi project set refuses a member are among them, and unset has no plan token) and is not available to an agent: propose the removal in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project init stores a whole answers file (the models answers that choose the runtime and what counts as a barrier among them) and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set takes a path the guard cannot read here (it is missing, or comes from xargs, a variable, a substitution, a brace or a glob), and a models answer is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (models) changes which runtime the project uses or what counts as its barrier and is not available to an agent (qargi provider enable and qargi provider accept have a plan token). Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (the release answers, test_command, gates, env, upstream, verify.environment, the site answers, backlog.file) changes a command or an environment the lead later runs, the remote it fetches from or the site it builds or the file that qargi backlog done rewrites and is not available to an agent: propose the value in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (runs) declares which refs verify and clean accept as created by a runtime (runs.owned_refs), a way round the ref check of a run, and is not available to an agent: propose the pattern in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (packs) opts the project out of the packs render check (packs.none) and is not available to an agent: propose the value in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (git.author, review.*) changes whose name the commits qargi review apply puts on a member's work (git.author, review.keep_author), or the scrub command and trailer policy qargi review check runs on a returned series (review.scrub, review.trailer_policy: the command is the lead's, run with its rights), and is not available to an agent: propose the value in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi project set of PATH (roles.ROLE.tools) changes the tools the lead later installs and checks out (roles.<role>.tools: go install, a downloaded binary, a submodule) and is not available to an agent: propose the entry in your report. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi provider accept records that you accept a provider with no read-only barrier and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi provider check records what it verified of a library pack (and may run the pack's code) and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi provider adapter-run runs the adapter of a runtime, and with --check makes a private copy of a library adapter, and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi provider VERB changes the provider definitions and is not available to an agent. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi AREA verify with --waive-environment and --approved waives a part of verify.environment with the owner's words (a flag the guard cannot read could be either) and is not available to an agent; report the refusal and the plan token it printed instead.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release site commits the built documentation site on the lead's site branch and is not available to an agent; report that the site of the release needs building. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release sign signs the release files with the lead's key, whose passphrase only the person types, and is not available to an agent; report that the tag needs signing. [member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release assets runs the project's release.assets_command, which is project code, with the lead's rights, and is not available to an agent; report that the release files need building. [member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release fix makes a worktree on the release branch and can push it with the lead's credentials, and is not available to an agent; report the fix the release branch needs. [member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release step marks an after-release step done in the lead's record of the release and is not available to an agent; report in your task output that the step needs recording. [member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi release publish creates a GitHub release and is not available to an agent; report that the tag needs publishing. Only a person, through qargi's own skills, changes a skill; propose the change in your report.

[member-lead-verb] qargi guard: qargi feature park resets the parking branch to develop and checks it out in the main checkout (and journals the move), which is the lead's to do; report in your task output that the main checkout needs parking.

next.host: stop: this session is not the holder; tell the owner

previous-epoch.message: {verb} is refused: this session holds the seat of an earlier epoch

next.host: stop: the seat moved on; tell the owner

projection-stale.why: a write must not run on a projection that has not caught up
projection-stale.message: {verb} is refused: the projection of the seat is older than the assignment

next.host: wait until the projection is current, then run the verb again; read-only verbs still run

next.host: finish the transfer with its own verbs, or wait for it to end

readback-pending.message: {verb} is refused: a read-back of the incoming lead is pending, so a lead verb that writes is refused

next.lead: submit or wait for the read-back, then run the verb again
next.host: submit or wait for the read-back, then run the verb again

seat-vacant.rule: A vacant seat is held by nobody who may write (R62)
seat-vacant.why: a project with no lead is looked after only by a caretaker
seat-vacant.message: {verb} is refused: the seat of the project is vacant

next.lead: ask the owner to assign a lead or a caretaker
next.host: ask the owner to assign a lead or a caretaker

not-assigned.rule: A verb of class owner is not run by an assigned lead (R59)
not-assigned.why: the owner's verbs are the owner's, run outside the lead's session
not-assigned.message: {verb} is refused: this verb is the owner's and this session is not the owner

next.lead: ask the owner to run it as qargi host VERB, in the owner's own session
next.host: ask the owner to run it as qargi host VERB, in the owner's own session

caretaker-denied.rule: A caretaker runs no lead verb that writes (R63)
caretaker-denied.why: a caretaker keeps the project looked after; it does not lead
caretaker-denied.message: {verb} is refused: a caretaker may not run this verb

next.lead: run only qargi env check, doctor, packs check or marshal caretaker request, or ask the owner for a lead
next.host: run only qargi env check, doctor, packs check or marshal caretaker request, or ask the owner for a lead

gate-error.rule: A gate that cannot answer refuses (R67)
gate-error.message: {verb} is refused: the gate of the seat could not answer, so the verb was refused

next.lead: tell the owner: run the verb again, and if it is refused again the gate itself needs a look
next.host: tell the owner: run the verb again, and if it is refused again the gate itself needs a look

seated-project.rule: A marshal claim, take or release is not run on a seated project (R27)
seated-project.message: {verb} is refused: the project is seated, so claim, take and release are refused

next.lead: use the seat's own transfer verbs
next.host: use the seat's own transfer verbs

assignment-invalid.rule: An assignment is well formed and names nothing reserved or unsafe (R4, R5, R18, R19, R28, R89)
assignment-invalid.message: {verb} is refused: the assignment breaks the rules of its shape, names a reserved value or declares an unsafe path

next.lead: correct the assignment and submit it again
next.host: correct the assignment and submit it again

transfer-open.rule: A new assignment waits while a transfer is open (R43)
transfer-open.why: two transfers at once cannot both be fenced
transfer-open.message: {verb} is refused: a transfer is open, so a new assignment is refused

next.lead: finish or abort the open transfer first
next.host: finish or abort the open transfer first

abort-after-fence.rule: A transfer cannot be aborted once the old lead is fenced (R42)
abort-after-fence.message: {verb} is refused: the transfer is past the fence and cannot be aborted

next.lead: complete the transfer
next.host: complete the transfer

fence-required.rule: A transfer goes past the fence only with an accepted fence (R36)
fence-required.why: the old lead must be proven ended first
fence-required.message: {verb} is refused: the step needs an accepted fence and there is none

next.lead: record the fence, then take the step
next.host: record the fence, then take the step

fence-unproven.rule: A fence proves the end of this epoch (R20, R29)
fence-unproven.why: a fence that proves nothing lets two leads write
fence-unproven.message: {verb} is refused: the fence does not prove the end of this epoch

next.lead: give a fence the transition allows, with proof
next.host: give a fence the transition allows, with proof

readback-mismatch.rule: The read-back matches what the project says (R49)
readback-mismatch.why: the incoming lead must believe what is true
readback-mismatch.message: {verb} is refused: the read-back does not match

next.lead: read again from the stored records and submit the new read-back
next.host: read again from the stored records and submit the new read-back

readback-exhausted.rule: A transfer allows three failed read-backs (R39)
readback-exhausted.why: a lead that cannot read the project should not take it
readback-exhausted.message: {verb} is refused: a third read-back failed

next.lead: the owner decides: abort the transfer or assign again
next.host: the owner decides: abort the transfer or assign again

note-digest-mismatch.rule: The handoff note is the one recorded (R41, R47)
note-digest-mismatch.why: a changed note is another note
note-digest-mismatch.message: {verb} is refused: the digest of the note differs from the recorded one

next.lead: send the note that was recorded, or record the new one
next.host: send the note that was recorded, or record the new one

note-invalid.rule: The handoff note verifies and belongs to this transfer (R47)
note-invalid.why: a note of another transfer or version proves nothing
note-invalid.message: {verb} is refused: the note does not verify, or names another transfer or version

next.lead: write the note again for this transfer
next.host: write the note again for this transfer

seat-changed.rule: A seat write sees the seat it read (R12)
seat-changed.why: two writers must not overwrite each other
seat-changed.message: {verb} is refused: the seat changed while this write was made

next.lead: read the seat again and repeat the write
next.host: read the seat again and repeat the write

refs-backend-active.rule: The shared refs backend and a seat exclude each other (R74)
refs-backend-active.why: the two keep the marshal's records in different places
refs-backend-active.message: {verb} is refused: the shared refs backend is on

next.lead: run marshal disable first, or leave the project unseated
next.host: run marshal disable first, or leave the project unseated

approval-refused.rule: A verb given --approved on a seated project is refused unless qargi host runs it (R76)
approval-refused.why: an approval is the owner's, typed outside the lead's session
approval-refused.message: {verb} is refused: --approved is given on a seated project outside qargi host

next.lead: show the plan to the owner; the owner runs the apply as qargi host VERB
next.host: show the plan to the owner; the owner runs the apply as qargi host VERB

authority-store-unsafe.rule: The authority store and the roots are safe paths (R8, R88, R89)
authority-store-unsafe.why: a store a lead can edit is no authority
authority-store-unsafe.message: {verb} is refused: the authority store or a root is unsafe or unset

next.lead: tell the owner: it is the owner's to repair
next.host: tell the owner: it is the owner's to repair

content-too-large.rule: A record is within its limit (R18)
content-too-large.message: {verb} is refused: the record is larger than its limit

next.lead: write a shorter record
next.host: write a shorter record

content-invalid.rule: A record other than an assignment keeps to its shape (R18, R22, R32)
content-invalid.why: a record that does not parse proves nothing
content-invalid.message: {verb} is refused: the record breaks the shape of its kind

next.lead: correct the record and submit it again
next.host: correct the record and submit it again

symlink-refused.rule: No path of the seat's stores is a symbolic link (R88)
symlink-refused.why: a link can point a write elsewhere
symlink-refused.message: {verb} is refused: a path of the seat's stores is a symbolic link

next.lead: replace the link with the directory it stands for
next.host: replace the link with the directory it stands for

caretaker-not-vacant.rule: A caretaker order waits for a vacant seat (R75)
caretaker-not-vacant.message: {verb} is refused: a lead holds the seat, so a caretaker order is refused

next.lead: wait for the seat to be vacant
next.host: wait for the seat to be vacant

host-in-sandbox.rule: qargi host runs only outside every sandbox, with a passed proof (R33, R103)
host-in-sandbox.why: the owner's own session is what the approvals rest on
host-in-sandbox.message: {verb} is refused: qargi host was refused: the proof outside the sandbox failed

next.lead: run it in the owner's own session, not in the lead's
next.host: run it in the owner's own session, not in the lead's

member-sandbox-off.rule: A member is dispatched only into a sandbox (dispatch)
member-sandbox-off.why: a member without one could reach what the lead holds
member-sandbox-off.message: {verb} is refused: the sandbox of the member is off, so the dispatch is refused

next.lead: report it to the owner; do not work round it
next.host: report it to the owner; do not work round it
